To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

librarians need to develop a good working relationship with faculty and be able to communicate their knowledge in a way that faculty can understand, and faculty need to be willing to share their knowledge with the librarian and to be open to new ideas.
librarians can play a significant role in teaching information skills and can be successful in this role by collaborating with faculty.

(1) faculty-library collaboration can be successful, but it requires a great deal of time and effort; (2) librarians need to be flexible and willing to take on new roles; (3) librarians should not underestimate the importance of the librarian’s knowledge; (4) team-teaching can be an effective pedagogical approach; (5) the tutor approach can be effective, but it may be time-consuming for librarians.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how librarians and faculty can work together to develop information literacy skills and knowledge.
the challenges and possibilities of embedded librarians and how these challenges can be overcome.
how librarians can collaborate with faculty in the classroom and how this collaboration affects the teaching-learning process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the librarian’s role is not only to be an expert in information skills, but also to be a teacher.
librarians need to be aware of the time commitment that faculty-library collaboration requires and that they need to be prepared for a variety of reactions from faculty.
collaboration between librarians and faculty staff can be successful and rewarding, but it is time-consuming.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the librarian’s knowledge, skills and expertise, and the ability to adapt to different situations and environments are crucial for a successful collaboration.
librarians should be aware of the challenges and the possibilities that may come with collaboration.
the librarian’s role in collaboration is to provide expertise in information literacy and to support the faculty staff with the teaching of this subject.
The main takeaway from our work is that
librarians need to be flexible and creative when working in a faculty-library collaboration.
librarians need to be flexible, and be able to work with faculty on their terms.
the librarian should be prepared to work closely with faculty staff and be ready to take on a more active teaching role.
